topic: The Great Molasses Flood of 1919 (story Reel, host Nea Costel)
title: THE GREAT
MOLASSES FLOOD

script.text: Boston, 1919. Lunchtime.
A sound like a machine gun rips through the harbour.
Then a wave as tall as a house comes down the street.
But it isn't water. It's syrup.
This is the Great Molasses Flood. And yes, it really happened.
On the waterfront stood a giant steel tank, fifteen metres tall.
Inside: about eight point seven million litres of molasses, waiting to be turned into alcohol.
But the tank leaked. So badly that the company painted it brown, so nobody could see the leaks.
Neighbours came with cups and buckets to take the drips home.
Then, January fifteenth. After days of freezing cold, the air suddenly turned warm.
Just after half past twelve, the rivets started popping, like gunshots.
And the tank burst open.
A brown wave, up to seven and a half metres high, rushed through the streets at about fifty-five kilometres an hour.
It knocked houses off their foundations. It bent the steel of the elevated railway.
Wagons, horses, people. It took everything.
And here comes the worst part.
In the cold winter air, the molasses got thick, like glue. People could not swim out. The harder they fought, the deeper they sank.
Sailors, firemen and doctors waded in to pull people out.
Twenty-one people died. About a hundred and fifty were hurt.
The clean-up took weeks. Fireboats sprayed sea water to wash the streets, and the harbour stayed brown until summer.
The company blamed anarchists. The court said no: the tank was too thin, and had never been properly tested.
After that, engineers had to sign off on their designs. Rules that still protect us today.
So yes, twenty-one people drowned in syrup. That's real.
Next time someone says slow as molasses, tell them about Boston. Follow for more strange history.

science.claim: 15 Jan 1919, Boston North End, about 12:40 pm; tank 50 ft (15 m) tall held about 2.3 million US gallons (8.7 million L) of molasses for industrial alcohol (Purity Distilling / USIA).
science.source: Wikipedia, Great Molasses Flood; Boston Public Library

science.claim: The tank leaked; it was painted brown to hide the leaks; residents collected leaking molasses.
Temperatures rose sharply the day of the disaster after a cold spell.
science.working: from about -17 C to above 4 C

science.claim: Witnesses described a machine-gun sound of rivets popping.
Wave up to about 25 ft (7.6 m) at about 35 mph (56 km/h); buildings off foundations; elevated railway girders damaged; horses killed.
science.working: Wave heights vary by source; script says up to 7.5 m.

science.claim: Molasses thickened in the cold, trapping victims.
21 dead, about 150 injured; cleanup took weeks; fireboats used salt water; harbor brown until summer.
Company blamed anarchists; court found the tank structurally unsound and inadequately tested; led to rules requiring engineers to sign off on calculations.

harbour: a busy 1919 harbour street at noon, horse carts, distant ship horn, seagulls, crowd murmur, no clear words
rivets: steel rivets popping off a huge metal tank one after another, loud like machine gun fire
rumble: a deep low rumble growing louder, a huge thick wave of liquid approaching, ominous
burst: a giant steel tank bursting open with a metallic crack and a huge gush of thick liquid
wave: a thick heavy wave of syrup crashing through a street, wood snapping, metal groaning
creak: heavy steel girders bending and screeching under strain
drip: thick syrup slowly dripping into a metal bucket, sticky drips
brush: a paint roller rolling thick paint onto a metal wall
pop: a cartoon speech bubble pop, short and bright
gavel: a judge gavel banging twice on a wooden block in a quiet courtroom
stamp: a heavy rubber stamp slammed down hard on a wooden desk, one thud
sea_spray: a fireboat water cannon spraying, splashing water on cobblestones
night_amb: a quiet harbour at night, gentle water lapping, distant bell, no voices
score: cinematic documentary storytelling score, curious and slightly ominous strings and pizzicato, builds to tense drums in the middle, then calm and reflective, no vocals
